title: Fernbridge Manufacturing — Staff Handbook Extracts

texts.label: A
texts.heading: New Starter Handbook: Working Hours and Breaks
texts.text:
A
All production staff at Fernbridge Manufacturing work a standard 37.5-hour week across five days, with core hours between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. Employees on the early shift begin at 6 a.m. and finish at 2 p.m., while those on the late shift work from 2 p.m. to 10 p.m. Shift patterns rotate every four weeks and are published on the staff noticeboard no later than the preceding Friday.

B
Breaks during a full shift are arranged as follows:
- A 30-minute unpaid lunch break, taken between 12 p.m. and 1.30 p.m.
- Two paid 10-minute breaks, one in the first half of the shift and one in the second.
- An additional 15-minute break for shifts longer than eight hours.
Breaks must be staggered within each team so that production lines are never left unattended.

C
All staff must clock in and out using the card reader at the staff entrance, including for lunch breaks. Employees who forget their card should report to their supervisor within the same shift; repeated failure to clock in correctly may result in pay being withheld until hours are verified manually. Persistent lateness of more than ten minutes on three occasions within a rolling month will be recorded as a formal attendance concern.

D
Employees who wish to swap an assigned shift with a colleague must submit the request in writing to their supervisor at least 48 hours in advance, using the shift-swap form available from the staff office. Both employees remain responsible for meeting their required weekly hours, and swaps that would leave fewer than eleven hours' rest between shifts will not be approved.

texts.label: B
texts.heading: Leave and Overtime Policy
texts.text:
A
Full-time employees are entitled to 28 days of paid annual leave per year, including public holidays. Leave entitlement is calculated on a pro-rata basis for part-time staff and for anyone joining partway through the leave year, which runs from 1 April to 31 March.

B
To request leave:
- Submit requests through the online staff portal at least two weeks in advance.
- Requests for more than five consecutive days require four weeks' notice.
- No more than three team members from the same section may be on leave at the same time.
- Leave requested during the final two weeks of December must be approved by the department manager directly.

C
Overtime is paid at 1.5 times the standard hourly rate for hours worked beyond the 37.5-hour week, and at double time for work on public holidays. Overtime must be authorised in advance by a line manager; unauthorised overtime will not be paid. Staff who accumulate more than ten hours of overtime in a single month may choose to take the excess as time off in lieu instead of payment.

D
Up to five days of unused annual leave may be carried forward into the following leave year with written approval from a manager, but any leave not taken or approved for carry-over by 31 March is forfeited. Employees leaving the company are paid for any accrued but untaken leave as part of their final salary.
